exposure: Planned delivery (elective cesarean section, vaginal delivery) vs. unplanned delivery (vacuum extraction, emergency cesarean section)
Intervention type (vacuum extraction vs. emergency cesarean section)
Indications for intervention (arrest of labor vs. risk to mother or fetus)
outcome: Maternal childbirth experience (Subjective Childbirth Experience Questionnaire score)
cohort: The study included 469 women up to 72 hours postpartum, recruited from the maternity ward of one tertiary health care institute.
finding: Unplanned interventions were associated with a more negative maternal childbirth experience than planned interventions, and the indication for unplanned intervention (arrest of labor vs. risk to mother/fetus) had a greater impact on the birth experience than the nature of the intervention itself.
mod_finding: Planned deliveries (vaginal or elective C-section) were associated with a more positive experience than unplanned deliveries (vacuum or emergency C-section), but no significant difference in experience was found between elective C-section and vaginal delivery, nor between vacuum extraction and emergency C-section.
